scope: First 48 hours of System time-series collection from accepted F04.var02's fixed-128, 1032-hour simulation; all other result windows and simulation behavior stay fixed.

parameters.profile_requests: 21 two-wave BASE-01 and 21 BASE-02 requests at 48-hour spacing
parameters.system_replication_rows: two unit-specific TOTAL=Y, TIME=N, SNAPS=N rows unchanged

acceptance_hypotheses: One fresh guarded SSH0/GUI13340/mutex native run passes exact 31 populated-table roundtrip, zero converter errors, warning #108 only, source pins and local raw SHA closure.
First-replication event log is byte-identical to the accepted full-window parent; ResultSummary and all 128 Replications rows preserve full 1032-hour mission outcomes.

Only SystemResults half-hour aggregate time series truncates to exactly 96 rows over [0,48), each identical to the accepted parent's first 96 rows. Stock and Resource time series remain 2064 rows and agree with the accepted parent.

OUTRP report retains 128 unique replication IDs and two-unit System TOTAL controls. Per-rep System TOTAL values may renormalize to 48 hours and must be reconciled with the short System aggregate before interpretation.

Short-window System aircraft-hour integral and terminal state agree with the accepted parent's first 96 bins. Stock and resource short-window integrals are computed explicitly from the parent and child prefix bins; full-window aggregates remain unchanged.
Independent read-only replay verifies source, native closure, parent-prefix equality and bounded interpretation before publication.
limitations: This changes only a System collection window, not SIMPE, mission collection, stock/resource windows or the number of simulated mission waves.

A true 48-hour simulation and an all-entity short report window are separate contracts; the excluded diagnostic demonstrates that all-entity RCEND changes also change ResultSummary and per-replication metrics.
Only the first replication has ENLOG events; same-seed parent comparison is for this configured model and engine.
GUI visuals, cross-engine equivalence and other F04 variants remain open.
